header:
2 people invest **$100,000** at 35
Only the fees are different

vo.text: One percent a year cost Marcus a quarter of his money.

notes: Both invest $100,000 once at 35, nothing added. Market return 7% a year before fees; the fee is taken as a share of the balance each year, so the net growth factor is 1.07 × (1 − fee). Priya 0.05%: 1.07 × 0.9995 = 1.069465 a year; Marcus 1%: 1.07 × 0.99 = 1.0593 a year. Balances at 35 + n, n = 0, 3, …, 30 (rounded to the nearest $1,000 on screen): 38 $122,321 / $118,866; 41 $149,623 / $141,291; 44 $183,020 / $167,946; 47 $223,872 / $199,631; 50 $273,841 / $237,293; 53 $334,964 / $282,060 (gap $52,904, first above $50,000; at 50 it is $36,548); 56 $409,730 / $335,273; 59 $501,185 / $398,525; 62 $613,052 / $473,710; 65 $749,890 / $563,079. Gap at 65: $186,811 (≈ $187,000; also $750,000 − $563,000 on the rounded figures). Marcus ends with 563,079 / 749,890 = 75.1% of Priya's money, ≈ 25% less. 'Fees took' = the no-fee balance ($100,000 × 1.07^30 = $761,226) minus each balance: Priya $11,336 (≈ $11,000), Marcus $198,147 (≈ $198,000); fee dollars actually charged were $5,005 and $83,557, the rest is the growth those fees would have earned. Rows have no t: default pacing (rowsT 0, rowEvery 0.7, plus the 1.4 s event pause), so the stress test also covers the kit's own timing.
